The appellant herein is the Referring Officer in L.A.O.P.No.322 of 2007 on the file of Addl.
Subordinate Judge, Chengalpattu @ Kancheepuram District, which was filed by the 1st respondent/claimant seeking for enhancement of compensation fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer in Award No. 1 of 2006.

sentences.text: 2. Before the Reference Court, the said L.A.O.P. was contested by both parties and on considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Reference Court enhanced the compensation from Rs.3100/- per cent to Rs.52,320/- per cent.
The said enhancement was awarded erroneously by appreciating the sale deeds relied by the claimant, which were executed two days prior to the notification issued by the State.

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Therefore, challenging the said award, the Referring Officer (Land Acquisition) had preferred this Appeal Suit and prayed to set aside the award passed by the Reference Court in the said L.A.O.P. by raising the following grounds for consideration :-
(a) The judgment and decree of the reference court below are contrary to law, weight of evidence and probabilities of the case and is liable to be set aside.
(b) The lower court has failed to consider the value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer in Award No.1/2006, dated 27.07.2006 is at Rs.3100/- per cent dry land acquired.
The Land Acquisition Officer arrived at the value only after considering the land value from and out of 92 Data sales statistics collected by the Land Acquisition Officer.

(c) The lower court has failed to appreciate that the Land Acquisition Officer has rightly taken the Data sale of a dry land to arrive at the market value of the acquired land since the acquired land and data land are of the same.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (d)

The lower court has erred in enhancing the compensation exorbitantly from Rs.3100/- per cent to Rs.52,320/- per cent in violation of the procedures prescribed under the Land Acquisition Act,
1984.

(e) The lower court has failed to note that when large extent of land measuring 19.61 hectare or 48.43 acres in Siruseri village was acquired the market value has to be fixed from the sale of large extent of land and not from the sale of a smaller extent of land that too on a square feet basis.

(f) The lower court has failed to consider the value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer based on the sale of 99 cents of land instead the lower court has considered the sale of 8400, 7700, 8800 sq.ft. of an approved layout viz., Neethipathi Venugopal Nagar from a different village viz., in Egattur for the fixation of the market value without following the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in arriving at the market value of the land.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (g)

The lower court has failed to note that the Land Acquisition Officer has taken a relevant sale deed from the sale of land prior to Sec.3(2) Notification under the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of land for Industrial Purposes Act, 1997 dated 26.03.2004 and only after analysing all the transactions as per data sale collected by him and rightly fixed the market value at Rs.3100/- per cent.

sentences.text: (h) The lower court has failed to note that the acquired land was an unapproved house sites and hence, the Land Acquisition Officer has taken the date sale of a dry land for arriving at the market value by considering the sale of approved house site from a different village.

(i) The lower court has failed to consider that the data sale deed taken by the Land Acquisition Officer for fixing the market value is nearer to the acquired land and falls within 1.6 k.m. radius and whereas the court has considered the documents from another village for enhancing the compensation. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
(j) The lower court has failed to note that the documents relied upon by the Land Acquisition Officer for fixing the market value is within the same village, where the land was acquired.

(k) The lower court has failed to note that the documents filed on behalf of the claimant and relied on by the court Ex.C5 to C7, which are sale deeds of smaller extent of approved house sites from a different village i.e. Egattur and the date of execution of all the sale deeds are 24.03.2004 which is just 2 days prior to the publication of 3(2) notification dated 26.03.2004 in the village.
(l) The lower court has failed to note that in all the three sale deeds marked as Ex.C5 to C7 the vendor and the vendee are one and the same
and the lower court has failed to note that there is every possibility that the documents would have been created for the purpose of escalating the market price for the land acquired.

(m)The lower court has failed to note that the 3(2) notification was issued in G.O. Ms. No.29,
Industries (MIG-II) department https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis dated 28.01.2004 in respect of the acquisition.

Whereas the lower court without considering these Government Orders dated 16.03.2004 and 28.01.2004 in respect of the issuance of 3(2) notification considered the sale deeds dated 24.03.2004 which is after the Government Orders dated 16.03.2004 and 28.01.2004 for fixing the market value of the land.
(n) The lower court even though discussed various ruling has failed to give any deduction towards development charges at the rate of 50%.

sentences.text: (p) The lower court has failed to note that the burden of proof is on the claimant and the records available is not sufficient and relevant.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (q) The lower court has erred in not following the belt system as ruled by the Supreme Court when a vast area of lands acquired are involved in this case.
(r) In any event, the enhancement made by the lower court are highly excessive, arbitrary and unreasonable and the reasons given by the lower court are unsustainable in law.
3. According to the claimant, the appellant had acquired both dry and poramboke lands nearby villages of Siruseri to form an Information Technology Park at Siruseri Village.
Accordingly, his housing plot measuring an extent of 200 sq. meters in dry land in Survey No.231/105 was acquired for the benefit of setting up an information Technology Park.

But, while passing the award, the Land Acquisition Officer without considering developments and other amenities in and around the acquired lands, fixed a sum of Rs.3100/- per cent by relying the data sale deed, which is no way equivalent to the acquired land.
Therefore, he raised objections to receive the award passed in L.A.O.P. and sought for enhancement of compensation.

To prove the market value of the property https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis as well as other amenities in and around the acquired land, the 1 st respondent/claimant relied the data sale deeds marked Ex.C5 to Ex.C7 dated 24.03.2004,
wherein the lands covered in those documents are nearby the acquired land and the same was rightly appreciated by the Reference Court and enhanced the compensation, which needs no interference.
Hence, he prayed to dismiss this Appeal Suit.

4. To encounter the same, the learned Special Government Pleader would submit that as per the Government Order, to form an Information Technology Park at Siruseri village, the vast extent of lands were acquired in various survey numbers belong to different individuals, which comes around 2.81.0 hectares and to initiate the acquisition process, individual notice in Form 'A' and public notice in Form-B under Sec.3(2) of Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land for Industrial Purposes Act,
1997 (hereinafter called as 'Act') was approved.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, as per G.O. No. 10/Industries (MIG.2)
department, dated 16.03.2004, individual notices in Form 'A' were sent to land owners/interested persons under Certificate of Posting on 26.03.2004 and 27.03.2004.
The public notices in Form-B had been published under Sec.3(2) of the Act on 26.03.2004.
Thereafter, on hearing https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis objections from the landowners in the presence of officials, the Collector had issued a direction to the landowners to hand over the lands.
Accordingly, the lands were acquired from various individuals, thereby housing plot dry land in Survey No.231/105 measuring an extent of 200 sq.meter (4.94 cent) was acquired.
Regarding fixation of the land value in respect of Egattur Village for the purpose of payment of compensation to the landowners, sales statistics was obtained from the Sub-Registrar, Tiruporur.

Thus, 241 sales taken place have been considered for fixing the land value and after deliberations, after discarding many sale deeds, the The Special Tahsildar vs K.Chandra on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10420396/
4 sale of an extent of 50 cents of dry land in Survey No.100/2B has been sold out for Rs.7,50,000/-
Document No. 419, dated 27.02.2002 at Tiruporur Sub-Registrar office, which works out to Rs.15,000/- per cent or Rs.37,050/- per acre and the said sale has been effected in the vacant land.

sentences.text: This land is near to the lands under acquisition and found to be equivalent to each other and the correct value was reflected.
Therefore, the said sale deed was taken into consideration.

Accordingly,
Rs.15,000/- per cent or Rs.37,050/- per acre was recommended to fix the land value and the same was also been approved by the Special Commissioner of Land https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Administration on 19.07.2006.

Thereafter, after discarding the sale, in respect of fixing the value for the lands at Siruseri Village, data sale deed dated 20.10.2003 was taken into consideration, which is pertaining to Survey No.235/6B1 and 235/6 and an extent of 99 cents of dry land sold out for the value of Rs.3,06,900/-, which worth about Rs.3100/- per cent or Rs.7657/- per acre.
The said sale reflects the correct value of the lands involved under acquisition.
Hence, the said land has been taken as data land for the purpose of fixation of land value to the lands acquired at Siruseri Village.

Accordingly, a sum of Rs.3100/- per cent or Rs.7657/- per acre was recommended and the same was approved by the Special Commissioner of Land Administration, but the 1st respondent/claimant and some of the claimants raised objections and they have preferred petitions for enhancement of compensation by relying the sale deeds marked as Ex.C5 to Ex.C7 dated 24.03.2004, which is two days prior to the 4(1) notification.

The Reference Court also erroneously appreciated those documents relied on by the claimant and exorbitantly enhanced the compensation from Rs.3100/-
to Rs.52320/- per cent, which is gross violation of procedures prescribed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1984.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.

Heard and considered submissions of learned Special Government Pleader appearing for appellant as well as learned counsel appearing for SIPCOT and perused the materials available on record.
6.

Considering both side submissions and on perusal of records, the Reference Court has relied the sale deeds marked as Ex.C5 to Ex.C7 on the side of claimant dated 24.03.2004, in which the lands were sold at the rate of Rs.120/- per sq.ft., thereby the cent value at the rate of Rs.52,320/- was fixed by the court as fair and reasonable one.

But, as rightly pointed by the learned Special Government Pleader, those sale deeds Ex.C5, Ex.C6 and Ex.C7 dated 24.03.2004, admittedly, two days prior to the publication of notice under Sec.3(2) of the Act.
In fact, the Government had passed orders on 16.03.2004, however public notice in Form-B under Sec.3 (2) of the Act was approved on 28.01.2004.
Therefore, the acquisition proceedings starts in the month of January 2004 itself.

Hence, the Reference Court ought not to have considered the sale deeds Ex.C5, Ex.C6 and Ex.C7,
which are all dated 24.03.2004, two days prior to the date of publication issued under Sec.3(2) of the Act and the value fixed in those documents with ulterior motive in order to enhance the compensation.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Thus, those documents were created for the purpose of showing the higher market value of the land and to refute the real value of the property.

The Reference Court ought to have considered the sale deed executed six months prior to the land acquisition proceedings, but it has considered the Sale deeds Ex.C5, Ex.C6 and Ex.C7, which is pertaining to an approved layout viz., Neethipathi Venugopal Nagar, which would totally differs from Egattur village and fixed the market value of the land without following the guidelines laid down by the Apex Court as well as under the Land Acquisition Act, 1985.

Therefore, by relying the The Special Tahsildar vs K.Chandra on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10420396/
5 sale deeds Ex.C5, Ex.C6 and Ex.C7, which were executed on 24.03.2002, two days prior to the date of publication dated 26.03.2004 issued under Sec.3(2) of the Act and enhanced the compensation from Rs.3100/- per cent to Rs.52,320/- per cent, which is highly exorbitant and illegal.
The Reference Court failed to take note of the fact that for the purpose of escalating the market value of the land acquired, those sale deeds were created.

Hence, the order passed by the Reference Court is liable to be set aside and the alleged enhancement of compensation is exorbitant one and also violation of procedures prescribed under the Land Acquisition Act.
Accordingly, this https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Appeal Suit is allowed and the findings rendered by the Reference Court in L.A.O.P.No. 322 of 2007 is set aside.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Civil Miscellaneous Petition is closed.

7. Furthermore, Registry is directed to call for remarks from the concerned Judicial Officer for passing such an erratic award deliberately by violating the rules and without application of mind as it lead to miscarriage of justice.
